channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Bolsonaro Surges to Lead as Brazil Swings to the Right
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro led Brazil's first round election as voted were still being counted. A victory for Bolsonaro would accelerate President Donald Trump’s effort to reassert US primacy over the Americas after conservative allies won recent votes in Colombia, Chile and Peru. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sanchez Allies Said to Be Preparing for Early Spanish Election
item.description: Spanish government officials are preparing for an early election, pending a possibly imminent decision by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Bolsonaro Vaults to Lead Over Lula as Brazil Swings Right
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro unexpectedly finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election while conservative allies dominated downballot, setting the nation up for a sharp shift to the right.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho, Beatriz Reis and Simone Iglesias

item.title: Pentagon Redeploys Bombers From UK Base at Center of Terror Plot
item.description: The Pentagon has removed bombers based at the Royal Air Force base in the UK that was at the center of a suspected attempted terrorist attack last week.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: UK Tories Back Heathrow Third Runway After Burnham Demurs
item.description: Britain’s opposition Conservatives will say they’ll “do whatever it takes” to build a third runway at London’s Heathrow airport after Prime Minister Andy Burnham declined to support the planned expansion.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Jacob Reid

item.title: Schumer Demands Flock Delete Personal Data, Disclose Its Use
item.description: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer is demanding that Flock Safety delete personal data not connected to crimes and disclose whether federal agencies have accessed the company’s nationwide license-plate database.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Pro-Russia Dodik Hails Trump as Allies Win in Bosnia Vote
item.description: Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik, a supporter of Vladimir Putin and opponent of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s unity, retained behind-the-scenes power in elections and cited President Donald Trump’s influence for the outcome.
item.dc:creator: Jasmina Kuzmanovic

item.title: Taiwan’s Envoy Prods Trump Administration on Stalled Arms Sale
item.description: Taiwan’s representative to the US projected confidence that President Donald Trump would ultimately approve additional weapons sales to the self-governing island, which has been waiting for a $14 billion arms package.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: How Macron’s Decade in Power Left France Europe’s Weakest Link
item.description: Ten years ago, Roland Lescure quit a high-flying finance job in Canada to answer Emmanuel Macron’s call for an economic and political revolution in France. The banker was lured back to his homeland by the opportunity to turn back the rising tide of the far right and hand the next generation of leaders a pro-European, business-friendly bastion.
item.dc:creator: William Horobin

item.title: Justice Department Expands Election Fraud Cases
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Justice Department is expanding investigations into alleged election crimes ahead of the midterms, including noncitizen voting, and plans to deploy monitors to polling locations across the country. Speaking with Myles Miller, Blanche also discusses the department’s misconduct complaint against Minnesota federal judges, its review of the Federal Reserve headquarters renovation and the administration’s defense of its tariff authority. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Economic Concerns Loom Over Trump’s Midterm Push
item.description: Bloomberg White House Correspondent Kate Sullivan and Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Ron Brownstein are on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing President Donald Trump’s midterm campaign push as Republicans defend increasingly competitive races in states including Ohio and Alaska. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they examine how voter concerns about the cost of living, the Iran war and data centers are shaping the campaign as Trump seeks to rally Republican voters ahead of the Nov. 3 elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lula and Bolsonaro Face Off in Brazil Vote
item.description: Bloomberg Brazil Country Chief Filipe Pacheco is on Bloomberg This Weekend as voters cast ballots in a closely contested presidential election between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, with smaller-party candidates also competing in the first round. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Pacheco explains the importance of turnout, the potential for an Oct. 25 runoff and concerns about possible foreign interference as Brazil conducts its election. Bloomberg’s latest coverage confirms the race is tight and that a runoff will be held if no candidate wins a majority Sunday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi-Backed Yemen Forces Begin Operation to Retake Houthi Areas
item.description: Yemen’s internationally-recognized government launched a full-scale military bid to recapture all areas under the control of the Houthis following weeks of escalation between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Sara Gharaibeh

item.title: Brazil Presidential Election 2026: Live Updates as Lula, Bolsonaro Face Off
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: South Africa’s Zille Leads in Race for Johannesburg Mayor: Poll
item.description: Veteran South African opposition politician Helen Zille is the front-runner to become Johannesburg’s next mayor, a new poll showed, but she’ll likely fall short of securing an outright majority in municipal elections to be held on Nov. 4.
item.dc:creator: Alister Bull

item.title: Russia Vows to Step Up Strikes After Its Warning on Kyiv
item.description: Russia said it would intensify attacks on Ukraine’s infrastructure following a vow from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to double down on strikes against oil refineries, a day after Moscow’s foreign ministry warned that diplomats and foreign officials in Kyiv were in “mortal danger.”
item.dc:creator: Greg Sullivan and Olesia Safronova

item.title: Tories Eye End to UK Inheritance Tax and Childcare Cliff Edge
item.description: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is using her party’s annual convention to call for the end of inheritance tax and an expansion of childcare support to higher earners.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Latvia’s United List Party Wins Record 42 Parliamentary Seats Backing Kulbergs
item.description: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ party won a record number of seats in Latvia’s parliamentary elections, an outcome that should help him consolidate power at a time of growing security threats from Russia.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis

item.title: UK Government Scraps Controversial Plan to Curb Some Jury Trials
item.description: The UK government said it will scrap earlier plans for some criminal trials to be heard by a judge alone, watering down proposed legislation that had sparked strong opposition from legal professionals and some Labour backbenchers.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wright and Lucca de Paoli

item.title: Germany’s Merz in Kyiv: Reiterates Support for Ukraine, Warns on Russia
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced a package of weaponry for Ukraine as well as aid for the country’s energy sector worth about €1.35 billion ($1.5 billion) during a visit to Kyiv Sunday that coincided with Russia’s latest attack on the capital.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova and Iain Rogers
